newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures surge by daily limit.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures surge by daily limit.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures surged on Friday, with all contracts closing up by their daily 400 yen limit on aggressive buying from local investors, traders said.
The benchmark July 1998 contract was up 400 yen at 14,890 yen per tonne. Estimated volume was 97,218 lots.
Heavy buying from individual investors, who were mainly encouraged by the weaker yen against the dollar, emerged from the opening, traders said.
"The rally in soybean futures also accelerated the bullish mood of the corn market," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.65 per bushel at 0735 GMT, against $2.65-1/2 at Thursday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $7.67 per bushel at 0735 GMT, against $7.68 at Thursday's close.
